title: Joel 1: chapter overview
paragraphs: A plague of locusts. (Joel 1:1-7) All sorts of people are called to lament it. (Joel 1:8-13) They are to look to God. (Joel 1:14-20)
Joel 1:1-7 The most aged could not remember such calamities as were about to take place.

outline.text: A plague of locusts. (Joel 1:1-7) All sorts of people are called to lament it. (Joel 1:8-13) They are to look to God. (Joel 1:14-20)
Joel 1:1-7 The most aged could not remember such calamities as were about to take place.

context: From the desolations about to come upon the land of Judah, by the ravages of locusts and other insects, the prophet Joel exhorts the Jews to repentance, fasting, and prayer.
attribution: Matthew Henry, Concise Commentary (public domain). Historical Protestant interpretation; other traditions may read these passages differently.

title: Joel 2: chapter overview
paragraphs: God's judgments. (Joel 2:1-14) Exhortations to fasting and prayer; blessings promised. (Joel 2:15-27) A promise of the Holy Spirit, and of future mercies. (Joel 2:28-32)
Joel 2:1-14 The priests were to alarm the people with the near approach of the Divine judgments.

title: Joel 3: chapter overview
paragraphs: God's judgments in the latter days. (Joel 3:1-8) The extent of these judgments. (Joel 3:9-17) The blessings the church shall enjoy. (Joel 3:18-21)
Joel 3:1-8 The restoration of the Jews, and the final victory of true religion over all opposers, appear to be here foretold.
